sentences.text: Polesinesuchus was an extinct stagonolepidid aetosaur, a group of armored reptiles, that lived during the Late Triassic period.
The single known specimen is estimated to be 76 centimeters long and likely represents a two-year-old juvenile.
Its vertebrae lack hyposphene articulations, which are specific connections between bones in the neck and mid-back.
This species is the fifth aetosaur discovered in South America.
Named in 2014 by a team including Lúcio Roberto-da-Silva, the genus was described based on a holotype collected from the Santa Maria Formation.
The only known fossil material consists of a partially articulated skeleton containing skull and postcranial parts found within the Santa Maria Supersequence.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Polesinesuchus as the sister taxon of Aetobarbakinoides.
Close relatives of this clade include the South American genera Aetosauroides and Neoaetosauroides.
The animal lived during the Carnian stage, approximately 237 to 227.3 million years ago.

Originally, the genus was distinguished by unique vertebral characters thought to be independent of growth stage, but later research suggested these features fall within the variation seen in juvenile Aetosauroides.
Due to these similarities, Polesinesuchus has been suggested as a junior synonym of Aetosauroides.
